sections.title: Risk factors
text: Investing in our Class A common stock involves risk. You should carefully consider the risks described below, as well as the other information in this prospectus, including the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and our consolidated financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this prospectus, before deciding whether to invest in our Class A common stock. The occurrence of any of the events or developments described below could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations, and growth prospects. In such an event, the market price of our Class A common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations.

We generate a majority of our sales through third-party active independent agents. The over 14,000 active independent agents who generate our policy sales operate within a diverse network that includes independent agents, brokers, and referral partners. This distribution model exposes us to meaningful third-party risks relating to agent prioritization, agent attrition and sales productivity and competition within distribution channels, as well as regulatory and reputational risks. Competition exists for the services and allegiance of third party agents. Third party agents have discretion over which insurance products they recommend to customers and also represent other insurers. If our agents choose to prioritize offerings from other providers due to familiarity, perceived reliability, or regulatory incentives, or shift their focus to competing insurance providers based on superior pricing, more attractive commission structures, enhanced coverage options, or for any other reason, our ability to generate new policies may be adversely affected. …

sections.title: Use of proceeds
text: We estimate the net proceeds from the sale of shares of Class A common stock by us in this offering will be approximately $220 million, based on the initial public offering price of $12.00 per share of Class A common stock, and after deducting the underwriting discounts and commissions and our estimated offering expenses of $5 million.

The principal purposes of this offering are to increase our capitalization and financial flexibility and to create a public market for our Class A common stock. We intend to use the net proceeds from this offering as capital to grow our business and for other general corporate purposes. We periodically evaluate strategic opportunities; however, we have no current commitments for any material acquisitions or investments at this time.

We may also use a portion of the net proceeds we receive from this offering to repay $281.5 million of outstanding indebtedness under our New Credit Facility. See “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Liquidity and Capital Resources—Debt” for more information. Certain of the underwriters or their affiliates act as lenders under our New Credit Facility and may therefore receive a portion of the net proceeds from this offering.

On May 14, 2026, we declared and paid the May Dividend, which was funded with proceeds from the New Credit Facility. On September 3, 2026, we declared and paid the September Dividend, of which $49.6 million was funded with proceeds from the New Credit Facility. To the extent net proceeds from this offering are used to repay indebtedness under the New Credit Facility, such proceeds will effectively be used to fund the May Dividend and the September Dividend rather than to provide additional liquidity for our operations or fund future growth of the company. See “Risk Factors—Risks Related to this Offering and Ownership of our Class A Common Stock—Our management will have broad discretion over the use of the proceeds we receive in this offering and might not apply the proceeds in ways that increase the value of your investment.”

This expected use of net proceeds from this offering represents our intentions based on our current plans and business conditions, which could change in the future as our plans and business conditions evolve. As a result, our management will retain broad discretion over the use of the net proceeds from the sale of shares of Class A common stock by us in this offering and our existing cash and cash equivalents.

sections.title: Dividend policy
text: Prior to this offering, we declared and paid the May Dividend and the September Dividend, funded with borrowings under the New Credit Facility and New Revolver respectively. Both dividend payments resulted in significant payments to our principal shareholders, including Kenneth Gregg, our Founder and Chief Executive Officer, who, as the holder of a substantial majority of our outstanding common stock, received a significant portion of the dividend payments. As a result of the dividend payments, our total shareholders' equity decreased from $12.1 million as of December 31, 2025 to a pro forma deficit of $180.0 million as of June 30, 2026. Upon the consummation of this offering, we do not intend to pay cash dividends on our shares of common stock in the foreseeable future. However, in the future, subject to the factors described below and our future liquidity and capitalization, we may change this policy and choose to pay dividends. Any determination to pay dividends in the future will be at the discretion of our board of directors and will depend upon our results of operations, cash requirements, financial condition, contractual restrictions, restrictions imposed by applicable laws and other factors that our board of directors may deem relevant.

Our status as a holding company and a legal entity separate and distinct from our subsidiaries affects our ability to pay dividends and make other payments. As a holding company without significant operations of our own, the principal sources of our funds are dividends and other payments from our subsidiaries.

sections.title: Common stock reclassification and ass B stock exchange
text: We are currently organized as a Texas corporation under the name Orion180 Insurance Group Inc. In connection with this offering, we will file an amended and restated certificate of formation, which will become effective upon the closing of this offering (such time, the “Effective Time”). Upon the Effective Time, each share of our common stock issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time will automatically be reclassified as, and become, one share of Class A common stock (the “Common Stock Reclassification”).

Immediately following the Common Stock Reclassification and immediately prior to the completion of this offering, we will enter into an exchange agreement with Kenneth Gregg, our Founder and Chief Executive Officer, pursuant to which shares of Class A common stock beneficially owned by Mr. Gregg will automatically be exchanged for an equivalent number of shares of our Class B common stock (the “Class B Stock Exchange”). Shares of our Class B common stock will be entitled to ten votes per share and will be convertible at any time, at the option of the holder, into one share of Class A common stock. See “Description of capital stock.”

The purpose of the Common Stock Reclassification and the Class B Stock Exchange is to establish a dual class common stock structure in which Mr. Gregg will hold shares of Class B common stock with enhanced voting rights, while existing shareholders (other than Mr. Gregg) and new investors in this offering will hold shares of Class A common stock. Except as otherwise noted herein, the consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto and other financial information included in this registration statement are those of the Company and its consolidated operations and do not give effect to the Common Stock Reclassification or the Class B Stock Exchange. We do not expect that the Common Stock Reclassification or the Class B Stock Exchange will have a material effect on our results of operations.

text: If you invest in our Class A common stock in this offering, your ownership interest will be immediately diluted to the extent of the difference between the initial public offering price per share of Class A common stock and the pro forma as adjusted net tangible book value (deficit) per share of our Class A common stock immediately after this offering.

sections.title: Regulation
text: Our insurance business is subject to regulation and supervision in each of the U.S. jurisdictions in which it conducts business. U.S. state insurance laws and regulations generally are designed to protect the interests of policyholders, consumers, and claimants rather than shareholders or other investors. The nature and extent of state regulation varies by jurisdiction, and state insurance regulators generally have broad administrative power relating to, among other matters, setting capital and surplus requirements, licensing of insurers, insurance producers and adjusters, review and approval of admitted product forms and rates, establishing standards for reserve adequacy, prescribing statutory accounting methods and the form and content of statutory financial reports, regulating certain transactions with affiliates, and prescribing types and amounts of investments.

Many U.S. states have laws and regulations that limit the ability of an insurance company licensed by that state to exit a market. Some states prohibit an insurer from withdrawing from one or more lines of business in the state except pursuant to a plan approved by the state insurance regulator, which may disapprove a plan that may lead to market disruption. Some state statutes may explicitly or by interpretation apply these restrictions to insurers operating on a surplus lines basis.

The In-House Fronting Carriers are each organized and domiciled in the State of Indiana and are authorized (licensed) in the State of Indiana to transact certain lines of property and casualty insurance. These licenses are in good standing and, pursuant to applicable Insurance laws and regulations, will continue in force unless otherwise suspended, revoked, or otherwise terminated, subject to certain conditions, including the filing of an annual registration statement with the Indiana Department of Insurance (“Indiana DOI”), the primary insurance regulator of the In-House Fronting Carriers. …

sections.title: Management
text: Set forth below are the names, ages and positions of our directors, director nominees, and executive officers as of the date of this prospectus. The director nominees are expected to become members of our board of directors upon consummation of this offering.

Kenneth Gregg has served as our Founder and Chief Executive Officer since May 2015. Before that, from 2012 to 2014, he served as the President of Analytical Intelligence, LLC, an IT services company. From January 2007 to March 2011, he was President and Chief Executive Officer of Citon Group, Inc., an IT solutions company, where he created programs to cover catastrophic property risk while working closely with parties at Lloyd’s of London as an authorized cover holder. From 2002 to 2005, Mr. Gregg was the Executive Sales and Marketing Director for AXA Distributors, an insurance company, where he contributed to the company’s growth for two consecutive years. Prior to his role at AXA Distributors, Mr. Gregg worked at State Street Research from 2001 to 2002, where he was responsible for building an underperforming region into a sustainable profitable territory. Mr. Gregg’s early career involved roles as Vice President and National Relationship Manager for both Allianz and CNA, leading product distribution in the United States for those organizations. Mr. Gregg holds a Bachelor of Science in Economics and a Master of Business Administration in Finance from the University of Central Florida, and served honorably in the United States Marine Corps.

We believe Mr. Gregg’s qualifications to serve on our board of directors include his extensive experience in the insurance and financial services sectors and prior leadership roles in other companies.

Nevertheless, future sales of substantial amounts of shares of our Class A common stock, including shares issued upon the exercise of outstanding options or upon conversion of our Class B common stock, in the public market following this offering or the possibility of these sales occurring, could cause the prevailing market price for our Class A common stock to fall or impair our ability to raise equity capital in the future.

Upon completion of this offering, we will have 39,097,192 shares of Class A common stock outstanding and 59,935,260 shares of Class B common stock outstanding. Of these shares, all of the shares of our Class A common stock sold in this offering will be freely tradable without restriction under the Securities Act, except shares purchased by our affiliates (as that term is defined in Rule 144 under the Securities Act).

The remaining 19,002,852 shares of our Class A common stock held by existing shareholders will be “restricted securities” within the meaning of Rule 144 and may not be sold in the absence of registration under the Securities Act unless an exemption from registration is available, including the exemptions contained in Rule 144. text: The following discussion is a summary of the material U.S. federal income tax considerations to Non-U.S. Holders (as defined below) of the purchase, ownership, and disposition of our Class A common stock issued pursuant to this offering, but does not purport to be a complete analysis of all potential tax effects. The effects of other U.S. federal tax laws, such as estate and gift tax laws, and any applicable state, local, or non-U.S. tax laws are not discussed. This discussion is based on the U.S. Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “Code”), Treasury Regulations promulgated thereunder, judicial decisions, and published rulings and administrative pronouncements of the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (the “IRS”), in each case in effect as of the date hereof. These authorities may change or be subject to differing interpretations. Any such change or differing interpretation may be applied retroactively in a manner that could adversely affect a Non-U.S. Holder. We have not sought and will not seek any rulings from the IRS regarding the matters discussed below. There can be no assurance the IRS or a court will not take a contrary position to that discussed below regarding the tax consequences of the purchase, ownership, and disposition of our Class A common stock.

This discussion is limited to Non-U.S. Holders that hold our Class A common stock as a “capital asset” within the meaning of Section 1221 of the Code (generally, property held for investment). sections.title: Note 9 - Reinsurance
text: In order to limit the Company’s potential exposure to individual risks and catastrophic events, the Company purchases reinsurance from third party reinsurers through various types of ceding arrangements including catastrophe excess of loss and quota share treaties. The Company purchases reinsurance from various authorized and domestic reinsurers. All reinsurers with an unsecured recoverable have an A.M. Best Company, Inc. rating of “A-” or better or were fully collateralized.

The Company remains contingently liable in the event the reinsuring companies do not meet their obligations under these reinsurance contracts. Given the quality of the reinsuring companies, management believes this possibility to be remote. See Note 8 – Liability For Unpaid Losses and Loss Adjustment Expenses for recoveries due from reinsurers relating to paid and unpaid losses and LAE under these treaties.
The following is a summary of the Company’s reinsurance program:
Catastrophe excess of loss treaties provide per-event reinsurance coverage up to a stated limit in excess of the insurance companies’ individual retentions covering the period June 1 through May 31.

The 2025-2026 reinsurance program provides first event coverage on ultimate net losses up to $845,000 in excess of $35,000. SAA reinsurance supplements our 2025-2026 reinsurance program, which when combined with our quota share reinsurance, results in a first event ultimate net loss retention of $1,500 for OIC and OSI.
The 2024-2025 reinsurance program provides first event coverage on ultimate net losses up to $672,500 in excess of $19,000.

The Company enters into reinstatement premium protection treaties each year that are effective covering the period June 1 through May 31. The reinstatement premium protection agreements reinsure the reinstatement premium payment obligations which accrue under the commercial catastrophe excess of loss agreements for first event coverage.

sections.title: Note 18 - Subsequent events
text: The Company was named as a defendant in a lawsuit with an unrelated fronting carrier for a breach of contract. As of the first quarter of 2023, the program administration agreement with the unrelated fronting carrier was cancelled. As of December 31, 2025, based on the facts and circumstances existing at that time and the advice of external legal counsel, the Company believed it had meritorious defenses to the claim. Consequently, management determined that an adverse outcome was neither probable nor reasonably estimable.

Subsequent to December 31, 2025, the Company substantially agreed to a settlement (the “Settlement”) with an unrelated fronting partner. As a result, the Company recognized a $6,250 Settlement loss contingency within accounts payable and other liabilities and general and administrative expenses on the
Balance Sheet and Statement of Operations, respectively. The Settlement amount and outside counsel fees are substantially covered under the Company’s errors and omissions policy.

No insurance recovery asset has been recognized as of December 31, 2025, or through the date of issuance. The Company estimates that potential recoveries from its insurer could range from $5,000 to $6,250 based on current policy terms. The Company will recognize any insurance recoveries in the period in which underlying contingency is resolved and collectability is assured.

sections.title: Note 10—"Long-term Debt"
text: The Company's long-term debt consisted of borrowings under its credit agreement dated December 26, 2024, which provides for a term loan, a revolving credit facility, and a delayed draw term loan maturing in December 2029 (collectively, the "Existing Credit Facility"). The cost of issuance has been capitalized and is being amortized over the lifetime of the term of the loan. The credit agreement requires OIG to repay interest at a rate of SOFR plus a base rate, and $1,750 in principal per quarter. The shares of the Company’s subsidiaries excluding OIC and OSI were pledged to the issuer of the loan.
New Credit Facility

On May 14, 2026, the Company entered into a credit agreement establishing a $200,000 term loan ("New Term Loan") and a $100,000 revolver ("New Revolver") (collectively, the “New Credit Facility”), both maturing May 14, 2031. The New Credit Facility replaced the existing term loan, revolving credit facility and delayed draw term loan from the credit agreement dated December 26, 2024. The Company

recognized a $1,873 loss on debt extinguishment and legal fees from the termination of the Existing Credit Facility, presented within Other expenses on the Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations. The new credit agreement requires OIG repay interest at a rate of SOFR plus an applicable margin. The shares of OIS, CITON and OTX were pledged to the issuer of the New Credit Facility.

groups.group: Risks Related to our Business and Industry
items: Our distribution model depends on third-party active independent agents, and any failure by those agents to consistently promote our products or the loss of any key agent relationships could adversely affect our business.
We have experienced rapid growth in recent years, and our recent growth rates may not be indicative of our future growth.
Our rapid growth may place significant demands on our resources, systems, and personnel, which could adversely impact our business.
If we are unable to effectively manage our claims adjustment process, our business, financial condition, results of operations, and prospects could be adversely affected.
Competition in our industry is intense, and if we are unable to compete effectively, our ability to grow and maintain market share and our financial results may be negatively affected.
Increased commission requirements from our distribution partners could have an adverse impact on our profits.

Because the revenue we earn on the sale of certain insurance products is based on premiums and commission rates set by our reinsurance partners, any reductions, volatility, or adverse trends in these premiums or commission rates could adversely impact our revenue and profitability.

We may be unable to continue purchasing third-party reinsurance in amounts we desire on commercially acceptable terms or on terms that adequately protect us, and this inability may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
We are subject to reinsurance counterparty credit risk.
Our actual incurred losses may be greater than our loss and loss adjustment expense reserves, which could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, and financial condition.
Our success depends on our ability to accurately price the risks we underwrite.
If we are unable to successfully launch additional products or expand our product offerings, including into new markets, it may impact our ability to continue to grow revenue.

Our ability to compete in the property insurance industry and our ability to expand our business is partially dependent on us maintaining our Demotech, Inc. and KBRA ratings, and may be negatively affected by the fact that we do not have a rating from AM Best.
Reliance on the Orion180 brand is critical to our success, and any failure to maintain or enhance our brand or any damage to our reputation could adversely impact our business.
We are highly dependent on the services of our senior management team, including our Chief Executive Officer.
We may not be able to attract and retain the key employees and highly skilled people we need to support our business.
If we cannot maintain the valuable aspects of our Company’s culture as we grow, our business may be harmed.

Unexpected changes in the interpretation of our coverage or provisions, including loss limitations and exclusions in our policies, could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
We may be unable to prevent, monitor or detect fraudulent activity, including policy acquisitions or payments of claims that are fraudulent in nature.
If actual renewals of our existing contracts do not meet expectations, our written premiums in future years and our future results of operations and prospects could be adversely affected.
We may act based on inaccurate or incomplete information regarding the policies we underwrite.

We use analytical models to assist our decision making in key areas such as underwriting, claims, reserving, and catastrophe risks but actual results could differ from the model outputs and related analyses.

Excessive risk-taking acts by employees, agents, or third parties, could negatively impact our financial condition and business, leading to potential financial loss, business disruption, regulatory assessments, and reputational harm.

If we are unable to apply technology effectively in driving value for our clients through technology-based solutions or gain internal efficiencies and effective internal controls through the application of technology and related tools, our operating results, client relationships, growth, and compliance programs could b
Business or asset acquisitions and dispositions may expose us to certain risks.

groups.group: Risks Related to the Market and Economic Conditions
items: An overall decline in the housing market or general economic conditions could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
We may be negatively affected by the cyclicality of the markets and industry in which we operate.

Adverse economic factors, including recession, inflation, periods of high unemployment, or lower economic activity could result in the sale of fewer policies than expected or an increase in frequency or severity of claims and premium defaults, and even the falsification of claims, or a combination of these effects, whi

Severe weather conditions, including the effects of climate change, catastrophes, pandemics, as well as man-made events may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Performance of our investment portfolio is subject to a variety of investment risks that may adversely affect our financial results.

We are subject to extensive regulation, which may adversely affect our ability to achieve our business objectives. In addition, if we fail to comply with these regulations, we may be subject to penalties, including fines and suspensions, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of opera

The fees charged by our Service Companies to our In-House Fronting Carriers are subject to regulatory review and approval, and our failure to obtain and maintain such approvals may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Our In-House Fronting Carriers are subject to minimum capital and surplus requirements, and our failure to meet these requirements could subject us to regulatory action.
State insurance regulators impose additional reporting requirements regarding enterprise risk on insurance holding company systems, with which we must comply as an insurance holding company.

Changes to the E&S lines regulatory landscape, or a requirement for the In-House Fronting Carriers to file admitted rates for certain of its products, could have a detrimental impact to our sales, innovation, and ability to grow.
Compliance with insurance licensing requirements is critical to our operations, and any failure to maintain required licenses could disrupt our business.
State regulations limiting rate increases and requiring us to underwrite business in certain areas are beyond our control and may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
We may become subject to additional government or market regulations which may have an adverse impact on our business.
Changes in tax laws may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Applicable insurance laws may make it difficult to effect a change of control.
Our business is subject to risks related to legal, governmental, and regulatory proceedings.

groups.group: Risks Related to Intellectual Property, Data, and Cybersecurity
items: We are subject to stringent and changing federal and state privacy and data security laws, regulations, and standards related to data privacy and security. Our actual or perceived failure to comply with such obligations could harm our reputation, subject us to significant fines and liability, or adversely affect our bu

If we or our third-party providers fail to protect confidential information and/or experience data security incidents, there may be damage to our brand and reputation, material financial penalties, and legal liability, which would adversely affect our business, results of operations, and financial condition.
Any failure to obtain, protect or enforce our intellectual property rights could impair our ability to protect our proprietary technology platform and brand.
We may be sued by third parties for alleged infringement of their proprietary rights, which could be costly, time-consuming and limit our ability to use certain technologies in the future.
Use of our trademarks by third parties, and other actions by, or circumstances affecting, these other entities could negatively impact our business.

We employ third-party and open-source licensed software for use in our business, and the inability to maintain these licenses, errors in the software we license or the terms of open-source licenses could result in increased costs or reduced service levels, which would adversely affect our business.
Rapid advancements in AI technologies could increase competition and disrupt our business model.
Errors in underwriting or data modeling could harm our reputation, competitive position, and financial results.
We utilize AI in a significant manner through PryzmIQ and through our portfolio managers’ use of AI to scan for trends, which could expose us to liability or adversely affect our business.

groups.group: Risks Related to our Liquidity and Access to Capital
items: We have debt outstanding that could adversely affect our financial flexibility and subject us to restrictions and limitations that could significantly impact our ability to operate our business.
We may require additional capital in the future, which may not be available or may only be available on unfavorable terms.

groups.group: Risks Related to this Offering and Ownership of our Class A Common Stock
items: There is no existing market for our Class A common stock, and you cannot be certain that an active trading market will develop or a specific share price will be established.
Our operating results and stock price may be volatile, or may decline regardless of our operating performance, and you could lose all or part of your investment.

Because we have no current plans to pay cash dividends on our Class A common stock, you may not receive any return on investment unless you sell your shares of Class A common stock for a price greater than that which you paid for it.
If securities or industry analysts do not publish research or publish inaccurate or unfavorable research about our business, our stock price and trading volume could decline.

Our amended and restated certificate of formation includes a waiver of the right to trial by jury for any “internal entity claim” as such term is defined in the TBOC and, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, any other claim within the scope of the exclusive forum provision in our amended and restated byla

The dual class structure of our common stock will have the effect of concentrating voting control with Kenneth Gregg, our Founder and Chief Executive Officer, which will limit the ability of our other shareholders to affect the outcome of key corporate decisions and transactions, including a change of control.
The dual class structure of our common stock may adversely affect the trading market for our Class A common stock.
Texas law and our governing documents include provisions that may limit your ability to assert a cause of action against our directors or officers regarding matters of our business.

Provisions of Texas law and our governing documents could delay, deter, or prevent a change of control or changes in our management, which could adversely affect the market price of our Class A common stock.

Recent amendments to the TBOC have not yet been subject to judicial interpretation and the body of case law interpreting Texas corporate law generally is less developed than the body of case law interpreting the Delaware General Corporation Law.
Future sales, or the perception of future sales, of our Class A common stock may depress the market price of our Class A common stock.
We are a “controlled company” and, as a result, we are exempt from obligations to comply with certain corporate governance requirements.
Our controlling shareholder controls us and has the power to determine our affairs, including in ways that may not be favorable to us or other holders of our common stock.
We will incur significant increased costs as a result of operating as a public company, and our management will be required to devote substantial time to new compliance initiatives.
You will experience immediate and substantial dilution in the net tangible book value of our Class A common stock you purchase in this offering.

If we were to identify a future material weakness in our internal controls, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be harmed, which could have a negative effect on the trading price of our Class A common stock.

We qualify as an emerging growth company, and any decision on our part to comply with reduced reporting and disclosure requirements applicable to emerging growth companies could make our Class A common stock less attractive to investors.
Our management will have broad discretion over the use of the proceeds we receive in this offering and might not apply the proceeds in ways that increase the value of your investment.

notes.title: Segment Reporting
text: Operating segments are defined as components of a company that engage in activities from which it may earn revenues and incur expenses for which separate operational financial information is available and is regularly evaluated by the chief operating decision maker (“CODM”). The Company identifies its operating segments based on managerial emphasis and organizational structure. As of December 31, 2025, the Company has identified two operating segments: Underwriting and Services. The Underwriting segment includes a conventional, regulated insurance model focused on risk selection, pricing, and statutory capital management. The Services segment includes technology enabled policy servicing operations. notes.title: Variable Interest Entity
text: As part of the 2025-2026 catastrophe excess of loss reinsurance placement which incepted on June 1, 2025, OIC and OSI ("insurance subsidiaries") entered into a reinsurance agreement with SAA (also referred to as the "captive"). The captive is a segregated account operated by Wyndham Insurance Company Ltd. (“Wyndham”), a Bermuda Licensed Segregated Accounts Company that sponsors the captive. SAA is controlled by the Company and provides a layer of catastrophe reinsurance, see Note 9 - Reinsurance for details.

The captive was fully consolidated as the Company has the power to direct the activities that significantly affect the economic performance as well as the obligation to absorb losses and the right to receive benefits that could potentially be significant of SAA.
